chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: KDKA radio, the first station
summary: Hughes tells how KDKA started; she listened to music constantly.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: And that's the other important thing, Pittsburgh, of course, whether it was the Carnegie influence -- was the first radio station --

And I believe that started when an engineer at Westinghouse was doing some kind of research independently out of his garage in the nighttime when he used to broadcast records, have people come in to recite poems even over the air and then people would send him postcards to describe what

kind of a reception they got. He became so popular that the department stores realized that there was money to be made in selling little crystal sets.

Right, and of course KDKA being the first radio station we heard a lot of music because we got the local hotels who had bands and then of course, when they had the remote broadcasts, we would hear music from all over, you know. Especially late at night. So we used to listen to bands then. I think it was in the early '30s we used to listen to the bands from Chicago -- especially Earl Hines and Claude Hopkins and then the bands from what -- the Hotel Sherman in Chicago, and of course we had the Pittsburgh -- the William Penn Hotel. And the bands at the hotels would come on every day at noon and again maybe at 3 o'clock, again maybe at 6:00, and especially late at night.

So that's all I did after I got a certain age, was just listen to music. And of course it was then that I really began to aspire to being in the music business one way or another. I wanted to get away --
